description: Retrieve full scientific metadata for one or more samples by UID or SEEK ID. Returns metadata for the requested samples plus all parent and child (associated) samples in their full lineage. Output is JSON grouped by sample type; set output_format='excel' for an Excel workbook. Use this when the user provides explicit UIDs and wants comprehensive metadata including all associated samples.
llm_hint: Use when the user provides explicit UIDs and wants full sample metadata including all related parent/child samples. This is the correct endpoint for 'retrieve all samples associated with UID X' — not samples/{uid}/ GET. POST body must use field name "identifiers" (list of UID strings).
example_intents: Retrieve all metadata for SLD-230105ABC-12-PUB and its derived samples
Download an Excel spreadsheet with data for samples 12345 and 67890

description: Retrieve all assays (experimental procedures) you have access to. Returns assay titles, types, technologies used, and IDs for linked studies, samples, and data files.
llm_hint: Use for questions listing available assays or experimental procedures.
example_intents: List every assay record in the catalog

description: Return the sample lineage (hierarchy) around a given sample UID. Includes all related samples above and below in the lineage and the parent–child relationships between them. Returns graph-friendly nodes/edges (ID, UUID, sample type, relationships). Use for lineage visualization or when the user wants to see the full derivation tree from a specific sample.
llm_hint: Use when the user explicitly asks to see or visualise the lineage TREE around one known UID. Requires a UID. A question about that lineage (what a sample was derived from, what came from it, how many of a type descend from it) is graph_query. For full metadata export of associated samples, use admin/samples/retrieve/ instead.
example_intents: Show me the lineage tree around SLD-230105ABC-12-PUB
Visualise the derivation tree of SLD-230105ABC-12-PUB

description: Retrieve all sample type definitions available in the system. Returns a list of sample type schemas including titles, descriptions, and attribute configurations for categories like tissue samples, cell lines, animals, imaging data, and sequencing data.
llm_hint: Use for questions about what sample types or schemas exist in the system.
example_intents: What types of samples can I register?
Show me all available sample categories

description: Find parent samples that have derived samples of ALL specified child types (AND logic). Only returns parents with descendants matching every requested type. Optionally filter by parent sample type. Use when the user wants to find ancestors that have multiple specific types of derived data — e.g., monkeys that have BOTH flow cytometry AND sequencing data.
llm_hint: REST-path lookup of parent samples that have descendants of ALL the given child types (AND logic). A new lineage question is routed to graph_query, which checks each descendant type directly; use this endpoint for a refinement of a result that came from it.
example_intents: Same parent lookup as before, but add the imaging data type

description: Search and filter samples by type, attribute values, and free-text keywords. Supports multiple sample types, attribute-based filtering, and partial/exact match modes. Returns paginated list of matching samples with full metadata. This is a broad-purpose search endpoint — use it for attribute/keyword-based queries when no more specific endpoint applies.
llm_hint: REST-path keyword search over sample records: each term is a case-insensitive substring of any value, anywhere in the record. It cannot restrict a term to one attribute, AND two terms, compare numbers or aggregate. A new question about sample metadata is routed to graph_query; use this endpoint for a refinement of a result that came from REST, or when the turn must stay on REST.
example_intents: Same search as before, but only the slide samples
Run that keyword search again without the sample type

description: Search and filter samples from the Neo4j sample graph, limited to the caller's projects. Takes advanced_search's request body and returns its envelope (total, rows), with the same keyword matching and visibility, plus optional exact conditions: extensions.where (typed attribute comparisons on one sample type: =, <>, <, <=, >, >=, IN, CONTAINS, NOT CONTAINS, STARTS WITH, IS TRUE, IS FALSE) and extensions.lineage (samples with an ancestor, a descendant, or either, of a given type within 1 to 12 hops; for a caller who is not a superuser the related sample must be in one of their projects). total is the graph's count of every match; rows are one page read from the database, and can hold fewer samples than the page size when the graph still holds a sample the database no longer has.
llm_hint: REST-path sample search for what advanced_search cannot express: a numeric or date comparison on a named attribute, a whole-value match on a named attribute, or a lineage condition by sample type. A new question about sample metadata is routed to graph_query; use this endpoint when the turn must stay on REST, for example a refinement of a REST result that adds such a condition.
example_intents: Same slides as before, but only those with PercentNecrosis of at least 40
Keep only the chemical samples from that search that have an NMR data sample derived from them

request_body.sampletype: <sample type code, or a list of codes>
request_body.filter_searchText: <one term or phrase, or "" when extensions or sampletype carry the search>

description: List all investigations (research themes) you have access to. Returns titles, descriptions, and IDs for their child studies. Use when the user wants to enumerate available investigations at the SEEK level.
llm_hint: Use when the user wants to list investigations at the SEEK platform level. For questions about which samples are IN an investigation or study, use graph_query instead.
example_intents: What research topics are being studied?

description: List all research projects you have access to. Returns project titles, descriptions, and IDs for related investigations and studies. Use when the user wants to enumerate available projects at the SEEK platform level.
llm_hint: Use when the user wants to list projects at the SEEK platform level. For structural questions about project contents (what samples, studies, etc.), use graph_query instead.
example_intents: Show me all projects I am part of

description: List all registered researchers and users in the system. Returns names, email addresses, institutions, and IDs for associated projects and studies.
llm_hint: Use only when the user wants the list of registered SEEK user accounts themselves. A person named in a sample question (a lab or PI, or the Scientist who made or handled samples) is sample metadata and is routed to graph_query, never to this endpoint.
example_intents: List the registered user accounts in the system

description: List all standard operating procedures (protocols) you have access to. Returns protocol titles, descriptions, associated projects, and file attachment metadata.
llm_hint: Use when the user wants the LIST of protocol records themselves: what protocols are on file, their titles, descriptions and attachments. DO NOT USE WHEN the question filters, counts or analyses protocols -- which samples followed one, how many did, which protocol a sample used, protocols by keyword or lab. This endpoint cannot filter: it returns the whole list and the reply then has to admit it could not constrain it. Those questions are graph_query: the protocol is on the DERIVED_FROM edge as `protocol_title`, and samples carry protocol attributes.
example_intents: What procedures are documented for sample collection?
